title: More Veo 3 Sprite Animation Tests
author: Kulimar
selftext:
For this I generated various animations from a single sprite image using Veo 3 image to video in Flow and then imported the frames into Photoshop to remove the background. Ran a quick action to remove the white bg and tested it in a game I'm working on.

Would essentially still hire a pixel artist to clean everything up, improve design and overall aesthetics, but this is amazing for prototyping ideas!

replies.author: Kulimar
replies.body:
Steps:

1. Get pixel art you want to animate on a white or single colored background. 

2. Use Veo 3 in Flow to animate it however you want (keeping movement fairly simple and camera steady), 

3. Export the video from Veo 3 and import Video to Layers in Photoshop.

4. Remove the background in Photoshop (or whichever tool can do the same).

5. Export Layers to Frames

comments.author: IncorrectAddress
comments.body: Nice, these techniques are only going to improve with better models, there's still a way to go with AI animation.

comments.author: swizzlewizzle
comments.body:
There are an extremely small number of good examples of large snakes/dragons/non-humanoid pixel animations available, especially outside of heavily copyrighted game sprite sheets. It's likely that Veo 3 just doesn't have the training data to be able to get decent image -> video output if you feed it something that has wings (ie. wings need to move), has no arms/legs (snake), or a combination (dragon).

If you switch this to a basic humanoid doing something like swinging a sword or walking, your results will be very good.
